# Typer classpath corpus audit: Scala 3.9.0

The report is generated from the pinned Scala 3.9.0 audit, which runs once by default. Pass `--verify-determinism` to run it twice and compare normalized output byte-for-byte. It records first blockers for local method typing, isolated Match-case probes, PatDef attempts, and structural inventories. A moved first blocker is not semantic success. The source corpus, parser/namer setup, Scala revision, JDK 21.0.8 (feature release 21), and classpath remain pinned.

Run `tools/typer-classpath-corpus-audit/run` with the environment documented in `docs/typer-v0.1-compatibility.md` to regenerate this report.

## #1046 Package-term and module identity profile

Frozen 2749 package-term request observations across 80 distinct keys, and 369 module-related first blockers. Exact resource probes found 46 type-side `.tasty`, 51 type-side `.class`, 0 companion `.tasty`, and 46 companion `.class` target keys. The semantic TASTy classifications are {'class with companion object': 20, 'no canonical object evidence': 28, 'standalone object': 26, 'unsupported evidence': 6}. The blocker cohort is 361 `ImportQualifierNotFound` and 8 `TermNameNotFound` observations.


The [request profile](typer-classpath-corpus-audit-3.9.0-package-term-profile.tsv) preserves each observed package-term request and joins its exact `.tasty` / `.class` and companion-resource probes to semantic TASTy object evidence. The [first-blocker cohort](typer-classpath-corpus-audit-3.9.0-package-term-first-blockers.tsv) retains the 361 module-gap `ImportQualifierNotFound` and eight additional term/object `TermNameNotFound` observations with source method, direct/inherited attribution, exact failed qualifier, and request targets. Resource names alone are not classified as object proof. These are audit artifacts only; production resolution and typing behavior are unchanged.

## #946–#950 impure function hardening and next sprint

Historical #950 snapshot: the frozen #946 cohort retained all 13 method observations across 3 `FunctionWithMods` trees in 2 files, with the original one-argument `[Impure]` ordinary-arrow shape and 1 direct / 12 inherited attributions. The old first-blocker count was 13 / 2 files; after #949 it was 0 / 0. Per-row accounting in that snapshot showed all 13 stopping at `SymbolResolution`; none was fully typed. The source-type cache was rolled back with each enclosing failed method transaction, so the snapshot’s `projection=not_completed` column meant no projected root type was published after that method attempt. Focused source projection regressions verified that the impure alias was selected and preserved before normalization; the corpus result was bounded by symbol resolution. The figures and recommendation in this section record the #950 snapshot and are not recalculated by this script.

The full structural census still contains `FunctionWithMods` trees independently of first blockers. It also counts plain ordinary `Function` trees, which represent pure ordinary arrows in the parser. Modifier and family distributions, erased-parameter count, and `CapturesAndResult` adjacency appear in `function_with_mods_structural_inventory` below. Structural presence is not counted as a first-blocker failure.

In the #950 snapshot, the audit had 0 / 3,297 typed local methods. The #946 cohort moved 13 / 13 to the resolution/classpath family. External member requests rose from the prior 7,582 baseline to 7,802, while materialized external members remained 0; recent source-function and inferred-field cohorts also terminated repeatedly at `SymbolResolution` or `ImportQualifierNotFound`. The semantic rank was separate: anonymous class instantiation led at 32 / 15 files, followed by local type definitions and `SymbolSourceKindMismatch` at 11 each.

### Recommendation: import and classpath resolution sprint

The #950 snapshot recommended the import/classpath resolution sprint. It is broader than implementing anonymous classes, the highest single Typer-owned bucket, but it addressed the measured ceiling affecting the entire #946 cohort and multiple earlier cohorts: 7,802 external member requests produced zero materialized members, and 13 / 13 impure-function rows reached `SymbolResolution`. Anonymous classes were a bounded alternative at 32 / 15 files but required identity, owner, `ClassInfo`, and constructor/parent lowering. The compact semantic candidates ranked at 11 or fewer and would still have left the shared resolution gate untouched. This was a recommendation for the next sprint only; resolution implementation was outside #950.

## #802–#806 local extension hardening

The initial local-extension blocker was 25 occurrences in 5 files. The current audit splits extension-specific failures from ordinary local method signatures. It attempted 3,297 local method definitions and fully typed zero; moved failures are not counted as semantic success. Focused tests cover a fully typed local extension call, nominal-member precedence, local shadowing, unsupported receiver/signature forms, rollback, and bounded ambiguity.

| Focused extension failure bucket | Count / files | Representative paths |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `LocalExtensionGroupShapeDeferred` | 3 / 1 | compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/typer/Applications.scala |
| `LocalExtensionReceiverTypeNotFound` | 1 / 1 | compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/core/Flags.scala |
| `LocalExtensionSignatureDeferred::dependent result types` | 1 / 1 | compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/reporting/MessageRendering.scala |

Receiver or ordinary-argument mismatches remain non-applicable candidates and preserve `MemberNotFound`; the audit does not relabel those as successful typing. Multiple viable same-name local extensions produce `OverloadedSelectionDeferred` in a focused regression. Primitive definitions have no modeled member scopes. If nominal lookup cannot inspect a primitive member index, local extension resolution is not attempted and the original `MemberLookup` error is retained; fallback is available only after a completed index confirms that the ordinary name has no member. External member materialization remains zero.

### #929 local value baseline and #930–#932 implementation status

The pinned #929 baseline attributes 21 first-blocker observations across 8 files to 14 distinct `ValDef` declarations; none are `PatDef`. Five declarations produce repeated sibling-method observations, accounting for 7 observations beyond the first observation for each declaration; all 21 rows are inherited observations from the enclosing method attempt. The exact method/declaration pairs, source spans, full source modifiers, type form, RHS, visibility, annotations, and attribution remain in the historical #929 cohort below. Following #930, ordinary local values preserve `FINAL`/`MUTABLE` flags and contextual modifiers are validated. #931 types direct named `implicit val` and named `given` declarations, preserves their mapped flags, and inserts them into lexical scope after a successful initializer. #932 types direct local lazy vals through the same path and preserves `LAZY`; no runtime initialization or lowering structures are synthesized. Contextual search/insertion, recursive lazy type inference, explicit recursive lazy warning analysis, and forward references to later lazy declarations remain unsupported. Anonymous givens have no local term identity and report `LocalValueModifierDeferred::anonymous given has no local term identity`. The complete 21-row cohort is retained individually in `local_value_baseline_outcomes`: 4 rows stop at the anonymous-given boundary, 16 currently have `ImportQualifierNotFound` as their enclosing-method first blocker with no completed local-symbol mapping, and one inline row retains a focused modifier deferral. The current generic local-value blocker is that one `inline val` observation.

## Historical #825 MissingDeclaredType producer profile (pre-#856)

Before #856, the 34 first blockers across 15 files were all attributed to source `ValDef` declarations with a right-hand side and a zero-width synthetic inferred `TypeTree`. They split into 24 immutable values and 10 mutable variables; all have semantic `Field` identity. Source `val` versus `var` comes from the AST modifier and is cross-checked against the semantic `MUTABLE` flag; `SymbolKind::Field` alone does not preserve that distinction. The owner kind is `Class` for 24 occurrences and `ModuleClass` for 10. Four immutable module-class values carry `Inline`. Counts are downstream local-method first blockers, so one source declaration can appear more than once. The baseline profile is frozen here; current profile values are listed separately below.

### Family assessment

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Immutable `Class` fields (14 / 7) | Implemented in #854–#856; this report measures whether the corpus shapes pass the bounded path. | Field initializer context, ordinary RHS typing, widening, recursion guard, cache, and rollback are now covered by focused tests. | Full-corpus `ImportQualifierNotFound` movement remains a blocker; do not count movement as semantic success. |
| Mutable `Class` fields (10 / 6) | Implemented in #858; the pinned audit tracks all 10 source-method attempts individually. | Reuses the initializer context, RHS typing, widening, recursion guard, transactional completion, and assignment relation. | Corpus first-blocker movement is not semantic completion; module-class fields remain separate. |
| Ordinary `ModuleClass` fields (6 / 2) | Infer one non-inline module member value after class fields. | Reuse field type inference with a module-class owner and the namer-provided lexical context. | Singleton initialization and module cycles differ from per-instance class initialization. Keep module values out of the first slice. |
| Inline `ModuleClass` fields (4 / 1) | Add inline values as a separate follow-up after ordinary module values. | Reuse only the proven module initializer path and existing inline flags. | Compile-time constant and inline expansion rules add constraints. Do not assume ordinary runtime RHS typing is sufficient. |


`complete_symbol` reuses an already-complete symbol, and source type projection reuses a cached type-index entry before projection. #854–#856 routed eligible immutable class fields through the initializer context, normal RHS typing, widening, recursion protection, and transactional publication. #858 extends that same bounded path to mutable class fields.

## #880 literal singleton blocker profile

The #880 baseline audit ran twice at revision `777528f19a58e794c9954a42f433373472ec57f8`; normalized output matched byte-for-byte. Its 22 `UnsupportedSingletonReference` first-blocker observations all pointed to one source singleton tree and one enclosing declaration. The current values are reported separately under #881 below.

| Profile measure | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| total first blockers | 22 |
| profile entries | 22 |
| distinct singleton source trees | 1 |
| distinct enclosing declarations | 1 |
| distinct reference shapes | 1 |

All 22 were repeated observations of `val actionable: true = true` in `compiler/src/dotty/tools/dotc/transform/CheckUnused.scala`: singleton tree 2904, reference tree 2903, source span `[27444, 27448)`, and reference shape `Literal(Boolean(true))`. This is one declaration repeated through distinct methods, not 22 independent singleton declarations. Scala 3.9 and the dotty-rs parser retain `SingletonTypeTree(reference = Literal(...))` for literal references. After #881, supported literal forms project to exact `Type::Constant` values.

### Narrow follow-up boundaries

| Concern | Recommended boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Source type projection | Implemented in #881: supported source literals project directly to `Type::Constant` with the exact payload. |
| Type relation | Implemented in #882: compare exact supported constant payloads and relate constants to modeled primitive/Unit types. String constants compare exactly; String widening remains unsupported without a canonical source type. |
| Expected adaptation | Implemented in #883: preserve exact constants for singleton expected types, including singleton alternatives in unions; ordinary expectations still use the widened type. |
| Explicit deferrals | Keep `null`, class literals, arbitrary paths, unstable prefixes, and path-dependent relation changes unsupported. |

## #972 external resolution profile

This audit-only profile leaves resolver semantics unchanged. Request keys use stable semantic owner paths, namespace, member name, and member space, not per-store arena IDs. The raw report contains ordered per-method request keys and outcomes. The `SymbolResolver` contract does not carry subsystem/site tags, so the audit reports that attribution as unavailable rather than guessing.

The complete request-shape and outcome tables follow in the raw report. ### #974 TASTy parent-resolution result

The frozen #972 cohort had 342 `UnresolvedSupertype` errors across 33 requested classes and 79 files. After #974, 212 remain across 26 classes and 51 files; total member errors fall from 347 to 217 while requests rise from 7,895 to 8,070 as resolution proceeds deeper. The eight root families that no longer fail are `dotty/tools/io/AbstractFile`, `scala/Function1`, `scala/collection/AbstractIterator`, `scala/collection/IterableOnce`, `scala/collection/Iterator`, `scala/collection/SpecificIterableFactory`, `scala/concurrent/duration/Duration`, and `scala/math/Ordering`. Newly exposed failures include `dotty/tools/io/VirtualDirectory` and additional requests for `scala/annotation/retainsCap`; these are counted as remaining failures, not fixes. The 5 separate unresolved-class errors are also retained in the result.

The `tasty_unresolved_supertype_failures` rows below now include the parent index, structured shape, semantic-reference and explicit-prefix flags, visible name-table spellings, and compact raw-tree tag shape. A representative fixed row is `scala/Function1`: its `IDENTTPT` parent wraps a shared type reference whose target resolves through `scala.AnyRef`, still normalized to `java/lang/Object`. The real Scala 3.9 `Source.tasty` integration fixture covers an applied parent through the package-object alias path. Unresolved semantic references continue to fail without a same-package guess.

## #975 package type and member materialization

At the #975 checkpoint, package `TypeRef` plus a unique type name materialized a class into its canonical package/session identity. The pinned Scala 3.9/JDK 21 corpus recorded 358 external class symbols across 29 distinct classes (125 first materializations and 233 same-file session reuses); non-class external members remained at zero. The remaining member requests and errors are refreshed in the raw audit below. Focused fixtures cover a real JDK class and a real Scala 3.9 class, with complete class info, declaration scope, declared member access, inherited lookup, repeated identity, and rollback/retry.

## Frozen #976 audit gate and dependency profile

The immutable pre-sprint baseline (also retained in `docs/typer-classpath-corpus-audit-976-3.9.0.md`) used the pinned Scala 3.9/JDK `21.0.8` audit: one run was completed; determinism was not checked. The frozen #972 request shapes, #973 generic-signature cases, #974 TASTy parent cases, #975 materialization gate, and #946/#826–#829/#856–#858/#880/#899/#929 cohorts remain in the audit. The local-method result is `0` / 3,297. `ImportQualifierNotFound` is `2908 (277 files)` and remains in the resolution/classpath family; the separate Typer-owned semantic leader remains `AnonymousClassInstantiationDeferred` (32 observations / 15 files).

The `resolution_blocker_attribution` table in the raw output joins each tracked first-blocker method attempt to resolver requests made during its enclosing typing attempt. It reports cause, method count, file count, distinct target count and examples, and successfully materialized prefix classes. A cause is assigned only when there is exactly one distinct failed resolver target/outcome in that method attempt; no such request or multiple candidates is reported as `unknown` with candidate causes and targets. It includes `ImportQualifierNotFound`, `SymbolResolution`, `TypeNameNotFound`, `MemberLookup`, and `TermNameNotFound`. Package resolution probes distinguish an unresolved first segment/package from a loader error; member outcomes distinguish an unresolved package member, term/object gap, incomplete class identity, loader error, and other.

The external class-symbol gate is `358` successes across `29` classes; external non-class member successes are `0`, unresolved requests are `7493`, and loader errors are `217`. Package term requests have type-side resources for `2212` requests / `51` targets; companion `$` resources occur on `2196` requests / `46` targets. A resource is evidence only and does not establish canonical module identity.

The opt-in profile observed `958` top-level loads, median nested depth `0.0`, p95 `140`, maximum depth `141`, and maximum fanout `1048` distinct classes. The largest roots are headed by `dotty/tools/io/AbstractFile`. This distribution is evidence for an eager-loading tail, while the majority of requests have no nested dependency loads.

| Candidate | Measured reach | Reuse and risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. Anonymous classes | 32 observations / 15 files | Reuses ordinary `new` typing; high identity, ownership, and class-info risk. |
| B. Lazy/deferred dependency completion | `958` top-level loads; p95 depth `140`; maximum fanout `1048` classes | Reuses the new profile as before/after evidence; high loader transaction and completeness risk. |
| C. Package term/object materialization | `2212` requests / `51` target keys; companion resource on `2196` requests / `46` targets | Reuses package probes; high canonical module/companion identity risk. |
| D. External generic member adaptation | No corpus external non-class member has materialized yet. | Focused generic receiver support exists; broad substitution semantics remain unmeasured in corpus reach. |

**Historical #976 next sprint recommendation: investigate lazy/deferred dependency completion.** The p95 and maximum depth/fanout meet the measured condition for this candidate; retain the profile and require a bounded before/after reduction. Do not expand loading eagerness as part of #976. This is one recommendation; the other candidates remain separately measured alternatives.
